en.name: Milkfish
en.summary: Milkfish is the everyday farmed fish of southern Taiwan, sold whole, as fillets, and above all as the fatty deboned belly. Fresh it keeps 1–2 days in the fridge and 2–3 months in the freezer. Belly cuts are the fattiest part and spoil first.
en.pantry: Milkfish does not keep at room temperature. It is an oily fish, and deboned belly sold on ice in a traditional market has usually already spent time near the top of the chill range before you get to it — which is why two days should be read as a maximum, not a target. Take a cool bag, and follow the 2-hour rule once it is out, or 1 hour if the market is above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, on ice, in a container that catches the melt water, and cook it within 1–2 days. Belly cuts spoil before the leaner back does, so cook those first and keep the fillets a little longer if you must. Pat the pieces dry and lay them in a single layer rather than stacking, and store on the bottom shelf below anything ready to eat. Milkfish sold in a vacuum pack carries its own printed date, which supersedes this while the pack is sealed.
en.freezer: Milkfish keeps 2–3 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Vacuum-packed belly freezes very well — press out the air, or the fat picks up freezer taint and turns yellow. If you are packing it yourself, wrap tightly with no air pockets or ice-glaze the pieces first, and freeze flat in single portions so you can take out one belly at a time. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are about quality, and it is the fat that decides them.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge overnight on a plate, or in a sealed bag under cold running water. Never on the counter or in warm water. Pat it very dry before frying, cook promptly, and do not refreeze raw fish.
spoilage: A sour or ammoniacal smell rather than a clean, milky-sweet one.
Flesh that stays dented when pressed instead of springing back.
A yellow cast and a rancid, paint-like smell on the belly fat.
A slimy surface or cloudy liquid pooling in the tray.
tips: Cook the belly cuts first; they go before the back fillets.
Take a cool bag — market fish has already used up part of its life.
Freeze in single portions the day you buy it.
Press all the air out before freezing; the fat is what tastes stale first.

faq.q: How long does milkfish keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 1–2 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, on ice. Treat two days as a maximum rather than a target for market fish.
Yes, 2–3 months at −18 °C, and it freezes well vacuum-packed. Press out all the air, because the fat is what goes first.

faq.q: Why does the belly spoil faster than the fillet?
faq.a: It is the fattiest part, and fat oxidises before lean flesh does. Cook belly cuts first.

faq.q: How can you tell if milkfish has gone off?
faq.a: A sour or ammoniacal smell, a rancid note from the belly fat, a slimy surface, or flesh that will not spring back.

zh.name: 虱目魚
zh.summary: 虱目魚是南台灣最日常的養殖魚，整條、魚片都有，最受歡迎的則是油脂豐厚的無刺魚肚。新鮮的冷藏可放 1～2 天，冷凍 2～3 個月。魚肚是最肥的部位，也最先壞。
zh.pantry: 虱目魚不耐室溫。它是油脂魚，而傳統市場冰上的去刺魚肚，在你買到之前通常已經在冷藏溫度帶的上緣待過一段時間——所以「兩天」要讀成上限，不是目標。請帶保冷袋，離開冰箱後守 2 小時原則，市場超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。
zh.fridge: 鋪冰放 4 °C 以下，容器要能接住融水，並在 1～2 天內煮掉。魚肚比背部的瘦肉更早壞，所以先煮魚肚，魚片可以稍微晚一點。魚塊擦乾、單層平放不要疊，並放在最下層、位置低於所有即食食品。真空包裝的虱目魚有自己的標示日期，包裝完好時以它為準。
zh.freezer: 虱目魚在 −18 °C 下可放 2～3 個月。真空包的魚肚冷凍表現很好——務必把空氣壓出來，否則脂肪會吸附冷凍庫的雜味並泛黃。自己分裝的話請包緊不留空氣，或先做冰鍍，分成單份壓平冷凍，之後一次取一片魚肚。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質，而決定它的就是脂肪。
zh.thawing: 放盤子上冷藏隔夜解凍，或密封裝袋用冷水沖。不要放室溫或泡溫水。下鍋前務必擦得很乾，解凍後盡快烹調，生魚不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸或有氨味，而不是乾淨的奶甜魚味。
按壓後凹陷回不來，而不是有彈性。
魚肚油脂泛黃，並帶油耗、油漆般的氣味。
表面黏滑，或盤底積出混濁液體。
tips: 先煮魚肚；它比背部魚片早壞。
帶保冷袋——市場的魚已經用掉一部分壽命了。
買回來當天就分成單份冷凍。
冷凍前把空氣全部擠出；最先走味的就是脂肪。

faq.q: 虱目魚冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 鋪冰放 4 °C 以下 1～2 天。市場買的請把兩天當上限而不是目標。
可以，−18 °C 下 2～3 個月，真空包冷凍效果很好。務必把空氣壓乾淨，因為最先變質的是脂肪。

faq.q: 為什麼魚肚比魚片壞得快？
faq.a: 因為它是最肥的部位，而脂肪比瘦肉更早氧化。請先煮魚肚。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷虱目魚不新鮮了？
faq.a: 發酸或氨味、魚肚出現油耗味、表面黏滑，或按壓沒有彈性。
